assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle and the 2018 observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity opened an entire field of moire quantum materials. It is a discovery with clear originality and a large, still growing body of consequences, and it reads as a discovery rather than an accumulation of incremental results. From a microscopy perspective, the way atomic-scale registry and twist control determine electronic structure is physically striking.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model supplied the prediction and the Jarillo-Herrero group's 2018 transport experiments supplied the decisive observation, which gives a natural theory-plus-experiment configuration. Eva Y. Andrei's early STM and transport evidence for flat-band behavior is a real competing claim that this three-person configuration leaves out; a fair allocation is not fully settled.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups have reproduced the correlated phases with transport, scanning probes and spectroscopy, so the interpretation of the core phenomena is stable. The superconducting mechanism is still debated, which does not weaken the discovery of the phases. Timing is reasonable at roughly eight years.
uncertainties: Whether Andrei's contribution warrants inclusion at the expense of Bistritzer or MacDonald is unresolved.
The pairing mechanism of the superconductivity remains contested.
I am relying on my own recollection of the chronology and have not verified priority dates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Predicting and realizing a new topological class of insulators with protected edge or surface states is a conceptually original and lasting advance, now central to condensed matter physics and materials design. The experimental realization in HgTe quantum wells gave a clean, unambiguous demonstration.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele provided the theoretical proposal of the quantum spin Hall state, and Molenkamp's group delivered the first experimental realization in HgTe wells, which supports a clear three-person split. M. Zahid Hasan's ARPES work on three-dimensional topological insulators and the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal (not on this candidate's list) complicate the story. The three-dimensional theory and experiments could be argued to be part of the same discovery.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed by transport, ARPES and STM across many materials, with stable interpretation and wide influence. Recognition is timely, close to two decades after the key results, and the 2016 prize on topological phase transitions does not cover this specific discovery.
uncertainties: Credit for the HgTe prediction that falls outside the supplied names is a gap in the configuration.
Whether the two-dimensional quantum spin Hall effect and the three-dimensional topological insulators should be treated as one discovery.
The extent to which Hasan should displace Mele is a judgment I cannot settle from the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance and its large enhancement in crystalline MgO barriers made magnetic tunnel junctions practical, and underpin hard-disk read heads and magnetic random-access memory. The result depends on interface structure and coherent spin-dependent tunnelling through an epitaxial oxide barrier, which is the kind of problem where atomic-scale characterization is decisive. It is both a discovery and an invention, and its impact is large and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Moodera and, independently, Miyazaki demonstrated room-temperature TMR in 1995, while Parkin and Yuasa independently demonstrated large MgO-based effects around 2004 after theoretical predictions of coherent tunnelling. The attribution is contested and compound: the two-stage history means no three names cover everything, and Miyazaki's omission is a real fairness problem.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: more than two decades of confirmation and wide industrial deployment. Timely or even late, and the Nobel Prize in 2007 for giant magnetoresistance is related but distinct.
uncertainties: Miyazaki's priority for room-temperature TMR versus Moodera is not resolved by the supplied credit.
The theoretical predictors of coherent tunnelling are not on the list.
The balance between the two stages (1995 and 2004) is difficult to represent in three names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2004 discovery of a high-mobility two-dimensional electron gas at the LaAlO3/SrTiO3 interface, followed by interface superconductivity and electrostatic gating, created a new area of oxide electronics and emergent interface phases. It is original and has had broad influence on correlated-electron physics. I note that my own group has published on oxygen vacancies and interface structure in this system, so I am close to the topic and have weighed that when placing it below candidates I regard as cleaner.
assessment.attribution: Ohtomo and Hwang reported the original 2DEG, and Mannhart's group contributed the tunable superconductivity and much of the device-oriented work. This is a plausible three-person configuration, although other groups contributed to the superconductivity result and to the magnetic and gating results.
assessment.maturity: There is long confirmation across many groups, but the microscopic origin of the conductivity (intrinsic electronic reconstruction versus oxygen vacancies and intermixing) remained contested for years and is a subject I know well from the structural side. The discovery of the conducting interface is firm; the explanation is only partially settled.
uncertainties: Interpretation of the origin of the carriers remains partly unresolved.
Allocation of credit for the superconducting and gating discoveries relative to the original 2DEG.
I should declare topical proximity through my own interface-oxide microscopy work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realized the Mott insulator transition and fermionic and bosonic Hubbard models in a controllable setting, which established analog quantum simulation as an experimental field. The originality and lasting impact are high.
assessment.attribution: The credit is difficult: the theoretical proposal for the Hubbard-model realization (Jaksch, Zoller and colleagues) and the first Mott-insulator experiment, with later single-site imaging and fermionic experiments, are spread across more people than a prize allows. Bloch, Greiner and Esslinger cover the experimental side, but Zoller and Cirac provide the theoretical basis and a three-person experiment-only slate would leave that out.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and mature as a field, though the claim to solving open many-body problems with these simulators is still developing. Atomic physics has received frequent recognition, which is a consideration but not a reason for dismissal.
uncertainties: Fair allocation between theorists and experimentalists is unresolved.
The extent to which the simulation results have solved problems that classical computation could not.
Several distinct sub-achievements (Mott insulator, fermion lattices, quantum gas microscopes) might need separate recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation explains the flatness, horizon and structure-seed problems and made predictions for the near-scale-invariant spectrum of fluctuations that CMB measurements have borne out. It is a deeply original idea with great importance for cosmology.
assessment.attribution: Guth proposed the scenario, Linde supplied new and chaotic inflation that made it workable, and Mukhanov computed the quantum origin of fluctuations. Starobinsky's earlier work is not on the supplied list, and this is a substantial credit gap; other participants such as Albrecht and Steinhardt are also relevant.
assessment.maturity: Consistent with CMB data on the spectrum, but the specific inflationary mechanism has no direct confirmation such as primordial gravitational waves, and alternative scenarios remain discussed. As a committee member trained in experimental physics, I would regard this as less mature as a physical discovery than candidates with direct measurements.
uncertainties: Absence of direct detection of primordial gravitational waves.
Credit allocation excluding Starobinsky and others.
Whether the prize criterion of a confirmed discovery is satisfied for the mechanism.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Rydberg blockade and programmable atom arrays turned strong, controllable interactions between single atoms into a platform for quantum simulation and computation, with direct demonstrations of many-body states at the 50 to several hundred atom scale. The achievement is original and visibly consequential.
assessment.attribution: Zoller and colleagues proposed Rydberg gates and the blockade mechanism, Lukin's group combined blockade with tweezer arrays at large scale, and Browaeys and Saffman demonstrated blockade and gates with individual atoms. The experimental credit is spread over several groups and is not cleanly separable.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly progressing and repeatedly confirmed, but the field is still evolving and the final scope of the lasting impact is unclear. Recognition now may be premature compared with candidates whose consequences are already settled.
uncertainties: Credit among theory proposers and several experimental groups.
Whether the most significant results are yet to come.
Overlap with other quantum-simulation candidates may make a combined recognition a better fit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The qPlus force sensor and functionalized (CO) tips gave non-contact atomic force microscopy sub-molecular and bond-order resolution, an instrument-driven advance that I value as a microscopist. The Nobel criterion allows an invention, and this one changed what can be imaged on surfaces. Its overall importance for fundamental physics is narrower than the leading candidates.
assessment.attribution: Giessibl invented the qPlus sensor, while Gross and Meyer demonstrated the chemical-structure imaging with functionalized tips. This is a natural three-person split between the device and its decisive application, though Binnig, Quate and Gerber's earlier AFM invention and the contributions of other groups (including Jelinek and others) complicate the history.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted and reproduced in many laboratories, so the method is mature. The interpretation of image contrast (for example the role of tip relaxation and artefacts) has been refined and is understood in outline. Recognition is timely but the scientific reach is narrower than other candidates.
uncertainties: The relationship to the already-recognized AFM invention might make the prize appear incremental.
Contributions of additional groups to tip functionalization are not captured.
I am applying my own field preferences and may over-weight imaging methods.
